reconstructed-moment-4.title: dream to be a full time artist

reconstructed-moment-5.title: And then you're like, well, what if this looked slightly different? Or what if this, instead of a tulip was a daffodil? And let's try to achieve that. So it's kind of like sitting at the wheel and just like letting yourself adjust, grow whatever ideas and just see if they're achievable.

reconstructed-moment-6.title: Um, so my voice and style for mud, which it's kind of a funny thing where when I was learning to do ceramics, I was also learning about the body positivity movement.

reconstructed-moment-7.title: first times like seeing different types of different shapes of bodies. I think that that kind of just smushed into one. And I was like starting to make these like chubby shapes and they're literally called this is the Chubby Mug. reconstructed-moment-8.title: And I was like starting to make these like chubby shapes and they're literally called this is the Chubby Mug. This is the Venus mug

reconstructed-moment-9.title: I think those two things kind of just mushed together the learning clay and the body positivity.

reconstructed-moment-10.title: they were originally supposed to be kind of like an abstract like vision of, of people, like different bodies sitting, dancing, whatever.

reconstructed-moment-11.title: the style has grown into something that now is just like, fun.

reconstructed-moment-12.title: I, It started off as one thing, and now it's just like, I just want to make something that, like, makes people smile.

reconstructed-moment-13.title: I think physical mediums are so important because, um, it's a way of connecting.

reconstructed-moment-14.title: Like, there's something called the artist's hand where when you, um, hand-built something or we'll throw it, you can kind of feel where the artist's hands have been.

reconstructed-moment-15.title: and I think that that is very important because we, you know, in society, we're like, so becoming more and more disconnected to, like human interaction in especially, like, touch or anything along those lines.

reconstructed-moment-16.title: I think that it's so easy to desire so many things, um, that we actually don't need.

reconstructed-moment-17.title: Um, but also just the value of keeping something for a very long time.

reconstructed-moment-18.title: the pendulum is really swinging in both ways, where people are really like, I want a select few things that I know will bring me happiness in my house. reconstructed-moment-19.title: But not only that, but like, you don't need all of that stuff. Like, you could literally just get a couple things that make you happy.
